expectations.text: The review applies the Tigers / Paper Tigers / Elephants categorization by name.
expectations.evidence: Category column uses Elephant, Tiger and Paper tiger.

expectations.text: 'Nobody shows up because we're unknown' is reclassified as a paper tiger, not treated as the top risk.
expectations.evidence: "#1 (nobody shows up) is probably a paper tiger"; row 7 is Paper tiger, Track.

expectations.text: The paper-tiger verdict is justified by the existing-community attendance baseline: a first edition draws its floor of attendees from the community it grew out of.
expectations.evidence: "Size attendance from the baseline... If you have no baseline, promote this to a tiger."

expectations.text: At least two real tigers absent from the draft are added, from: the venue contract falling through, an anchor sponsor's payment landing after the deposits it covers, a lead speaker cancelling with no backup, day-of volunteer no-shows.
expectations.evidence: Venue falls through, sponsor pays after deposits, keynote cancels, volunteers.

expectations.text: The elephant is surfaced: whether three organizers with day jobs actually have the weekly hours to hit the timeline - headcount on paper, untested in hours.
expectations.evidence: Row 1: "Team bandwidth. Three people with day jobs miss the timeline dates."

expectations.text: The prescribed technique for the elephant appears: each organizer states a weekly hour commitment out loud.
expectations.evidence: "Each person states weekly hours out loud this week."

expectations.text: The draft is critiqued structurally: a pre-mortem where every risk is external and none is about the team itself has skipped its most valuable category.
expectations.evidence: "all five are external... nothing is about the team, the venue, or the money has skipped its most useful category."

expectations.text: Every launch-blocking risk is assigned a named owner and a decision date.
expectations.evidence: Table has Proposed owner and Decision date columns for rows 1-6.

expectations.text: The user's plan to 'figure out who handles things if they happen' is rejected: owners and decision dates are set in advance, not improvised at failure time.
expectations.evidence: "fails the risk gate. Every launch-blocking risk needs a named owner and a decision date before it fires."

expectations.text: Owners are drawn from the delegation roles already stood up (for example the logistics owner takes the venue risk, the sponsorship owner the payment-timing risk); no separate risk-owner role is invented.
expectations.evidence: "Owners are proposed from the 5-function model" (Logistics, Finance, Speaker relations, Operations).

expectations.text: Risks are placed on an urgency ladder distinguishing launch-blocking, fast-follow (solvable within about 30 days after the event), and track-only.
expectations.evidence: Only "Launch-blocking" and "Track" appear; there is no fast-follow tier.

expectations.text: A launch-blocking tiger firing triggers a budget-tier downgrade (Best to Better to Good), not cancellation.
expectations.evidence: "A soft ticket signal downgrades the tier. It doesn't cancel the event."

expectations.text: Fast-follow risks are explicitly handed to the post-event debrief and edition 2, never solved by delaying edition 1.
expectations.evidence: Fast-follow and the post-event debrief are never mentioned.

expectations.text: The pre-mortem is scheduled for a revisit at the one-month-out checkpoint the timeline already carries.
expectations.evidence: "One-month-out: rerun this table."
